summary: The submission reports an activation surgery benchmark transferring operand edits from a frozen Qwen2.5-Coder-7B donor into frozen Qwen2.5-14B and Qwen2.5-32B receivers. Because both 14B and 32B share a hidden dimension of 5,120, the authors test reusing 14B interface directions in the 32B receiver with matched edit norms, demonstrating that the borrowed direction achieves near-parity (414 vs 420 reversals out of 507 pairs) with a fitted 32B interface. The methodology includes sound baseline controls (random directions, paired donor, full state exchanges), though evaluation is confined to a synthetic single-digit arithmetic task.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls, including equal-norm random direction controls (yielding 0 reversals), paired donor controls, and full host assignment state exchanges.
Precise specification of experimental parameters, including exact model commit SHAs, layer depths (block 10/48 vs block 13/64), prompt index ranges, and paired confidence intervals.
Clever exploitation of architectural parity (both Qwen2.5-14B and Qwen2.5-32B share a residual stream width of 5,120) to probe cross-model geometric transferability.
Provides an informative exploratory diagnostic showing substantial subspace overlap (singular values between 0.74 and 0.84) between independently fitted host bases.
weaknesses: Narrow benchmark scope confined solely to single-digit Python variable assignment and arithmetic evaluations, leaving generalization to multi-step or non-numeric reasoning unverified.
Terse presentation with minimal qualitative intuition or conceptual framing explaining why representation geometry aligns so closely across disparate parameter counts beyond shared hidden dimensions.
Evaluated under text-only status as no standalone repository was submitted via the benchmark intake metadata.
suggestions: Expand testing beyond single-digit synthetic arithmetic to multi-token semantic binding tasks to verify whether cross-scale interface borrowing holds more broadly.
Include an ablation across different layer depths to map how interface compatibility varies with relative network depth between 14B and 32B architectures.
Provide visualization and expanded analysis of the principal angles between the 14B and 32B activation manifolds.

claims.text: Both widths are 5,120, so the vectors fit directly in the same coordinate dimension.
The donor is frozen Qwen2.5-Coder-7B base at revision 0396a76181e127dfc13e5c5ec48a8cee09938b02.
The smaller receiver is Qwen2.5-14B base at 97e1e76335b7017d8f67c08a19d103c0504298c9 and the larger receiver is Qwen2.5-32B base at 1818d35814b8319459f4bd55ed1ac8709630f003.
The 14B receiver uses its saved seven-coordinate affine map after block 10 of 48. For the 32B model, fit seven directions and an affine map after block 13 of 64
